ing: 4 for the filling, 1 for the cheese mix
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[2 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tsp]] sugar, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Add [[0.5 cup]] yogurt and [[0.5 cup]] warm water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C). Mix [[2 cups]] mozzarella, [[1 cup]] feta, and 1 egg in a bowl.
Divide the dough into 4 balls and roll each into an oval about 10 inches long.
Add a quarter of the cheese to the center of each oval. Roll the long edges toward the middle and pinch the ends into a boat shape.
Place the boats on a lined tray and bake for 10 minutes, until the crust is golden and the cheese is melted.
Press down the cheese gently to make a well. Crack 1 egg into each boat.
Bake for 3 more minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are soft. Add [[1 tbsp]] butter to each boat, stir in the egg, and tear the crust to dip.
Mix [[4 cups]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt. Add [[1.25 cups]] warm water and knead for 10 minutes into a firm dough. Rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, pork, onion, cilantro, cumin, [[1 tsp]] salt, and [[1 tsp]] pepper in a bowl.
Add [[0.75 cup]] cold water a little at a time and stir until the filling is loose and juicy.
Divide the dough into 24 pieces and roll each into a 4-inch circle with thinner edges.
Put [[2 tbsp]] filling in the middle of a circle. Pleat the edge in folds all around, gathering to the top, and twist to seal.
Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook the dumplings in batches for 12 minutes, until they float and the meat reaches 160°F (71°C).
Lift out with a slotted spoon and sprinkle with black pepper. Eat by holding the top knob and bite, sipping the broth first.
Rinse the beans and soak in plenty of water overnight, or boil for 2 minutes and soak for 1 hour. Drain.
Put the beans in a pot with [[6 cups]] fresh water. Boil hard for 10 minutes, since kidney beans must boil to be safe.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 90 minutes until the beans are very tender.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onions for 10 minutes until golden. Stir in the garlic and [[1 tsp]] coriander for 1 minute.
Scoop the onion mix into the beans along with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Mash a third of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the stew.
Stir in the ground walnuts, [[1 tbsp]] vinegar, and most of the cilantro. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve warm, topped with the last cilantro.
Boil the spinach in salted water for 3 minutes until wilted. Drain and cool in cold water.
Squeeze the spinach with your hands until very dry, then chop very finely.
Grind the walnuts, garlic, and cilantro in a food processor into a thick paste.
Add [[0.5 tsp]] coriander, the fenugreek, [[0.75 tsp]] salt, and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper.
Mix the paste into the spinach with [[1 tbsp]] vinegar until it holds together. Add a splash of water if too dry.
Wet your hands and shape into balls about 2 inches wide.
Chill the balls in the fridge for 30 minutes so they firm up.
Top with the pomegranate seeds and serve cold.
Salt the eggplant slices with [[1 tsp]] salt and let them drain in a colander for 20 minutes. Pat dry.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the slices in batches for 3 minutes per side until golden and soft.
Drain the slices on paper towels and add more oil as needed.
Grind the walnuts, garlic, cilantro, [[0.5 tsp]] coriander, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a paste.
Thin the paste with up to [[0.25 cup]] hot water and the vinegar until spreadable.
Spread a spoonful of the paste on each slice and roll up from the short end.
Chill for 15 minutes. Top with pomegranate seeds and serve.

ing: or broth with 1 tbsp lemon juice
st: Season the lamb with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Place the lamb in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook with no oil for 10 minutes, turning, until some fat renders and it is browned.
Add the green onions and garlic and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in [[1 cup]] wine and [[1 cup]] water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Add half of the tarragon and cover. Simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the plums and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the lamb is tender and the sauce is sour and slightly thick.
Stir in the remaining tarragon and the cilantro. Serve with bread or potatoes.

ing: cut in pieces, or bone-in thighs
st: Put the chicken in a large pot with half the onion, [[1 tsp]] salt, and enough water to cover. Boil, then simmer for 40 minutes.
Lift the chicken out, check it reaches 165°F (74°C), and strain the broth. Keep [[3 cups]].
Pat the chicken dry and brown it in a dry skillet for 4 minutes per side. Set aside.
Grind the walnuts, garlic, coriander, fenugreek, turmeric, cinnamon, and cayenne into a smooth paste.
Fry the rest of the onion in a dry pan for 5 minutes. Stir in the walnut paste for 2 minutes.
Add [[3 cups]] warm broth gradually, stirring, and simmer for 10 minutes without boiling hard.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] vinegar and [[1 tsp]] salt, then pour over the chicken.
Let it cool and rest for 30 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature.

ing: cut in pieces, flattened or cut up
st: Pat the chicken dry. Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place the chicken skin side down and press with a lid or heavy pan. Fry for 12 minutes until golden.
Flip, cover, and cook 12 minutes more over medium heat until it reaches 165°F (74°C).
Move the chicken to a plate and pour off the extra fat.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in the pan, add [[8 cloves]] garlic, and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in [[1 cup]] milk and [[0.5 cup]] cream with [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thick.
Return the chicken to the sauce and spoon it over. Simmer for 3 minutes and serve.
Put the pork in a large bowl with the onions, [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, [[0.5 cup]] pomegranate juice, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Mix well with your hands, cover, and marinate in the fridge for 4 hours or overnight.
Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes if using them.
Heat a grill to medium-high or a grill pan. Thread the pork onto skewers, leaving a little room between pieces.
Brush the grate with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Grill the skewers for 14 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned and 145°F (63°C) inside, ideally higher at 160°F (71°C) for tender pork.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with sliced onion and pomegranate seeds.
Put the beef in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 75 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onions for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes and [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato mixture to the soup with [[2 tsp]] salt, [[1 tsp]] coriander, the fenugreek, and chili flakes.
Stir in the rinsed rice and simmer for 20 minutes until tender.
Mix the garlic, ground walnuts, and half the cilantro with a ladle of broth, then stir it in.
Simmer for 5 minutes. Taste for salt and serve topped with the remaining cilantro.

ing: tart green or red plums, pitted
st: Put the pitted plums and [[0.5 cup]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring, until the plums fall apart.
Press the plums through a sieve to remove the skins, or blend and strain. Return the puree to the pot.
Simmer the puree for 10 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in [[6 cloves]] minced garlic, [[1 tsp]] coriander, [[1 tsp]] chili flakes, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, and [[1 tbsp]] sugar.
Add the chopped cilantro and dill and simmer for 2 minutes.
Taste and balance with salt or sugar. Cool and keep in a clean jar in the fridge up to 2 weeks.
Thread each string through a needle and thread on 6 to 8 walnut halves, leaving string at the top for hanging.
Pour [[4 cups]] grape juice and [[0.25 cup]] sugar into a pot. Simmer for 40 minutes until reduced by half.
Whisk [[0.5 cup]] flour with [[1 cup]] of the cool juice until smooth, then slowly stir into the pot.
Cook, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until a thick pudding that coats a spoon.
Cool for 10 minutes so it is warm, not hot.
Dip each string of nuts into the mixture, let it drip, then dip again two or three times to build a thick coating.
Hang the strings in a cool, dry place for 3 days to dry, or overnight in a dehydrator at its lowest setting.
When firm and leathery, slice into rounds to serve.
